messages.subject: Re: Length calculation wrong for some genes
messages.subject_clean: Length calculation wrong for some genes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

Thanks for sending through the data.

When featureCounts reports exon coordinates in its output, it merges all overlapping exons for the same gene, eg. two overlapping exons will be combined to form a larger exon. For the case of Rgs1 gene, there are 30 exons included in your Gencode annotation and they were finally merged into one big exon due to the overlap between these exons.

However please note that the total exonic length and counts reported in the output are all correct, because your counting was performed at gene level (not exon level).

I now think it is not a good idea to report merged exons. We will modify featureCounts to let it output the original exons provided in the annotation.

Thanks,

Wei

messages.subject: Re: ERROR: BAM GZIP FORMAT ERROR.
messages.body_plain:
Dear Wei,

I ran into a similar issue while using Featurecount today. My linux platform has some kind of quota for data storage (100GB) and it was clear that the BAM FORMAT ERROR message resulted from exceeding this disk quota. After emptying the disk, a complete BAM file was created and the ERROR message disappeared.

Based on my experience, I argue that the BAM file creation is suddenly aborted when there is insufficient storage space. This renders alignment info only up 2 the moment when the break occured (f.i. 2/3 of the reads), but still a BAM file is created that is used for downstream counting. Was it not for the ERROR message during counting, I would erronuously have made my conclusions on the 2/3 of mapping reads.

A suggestion that comes into mind is to include a kind of "health check" of the created BAM file shortly after it is created but still in the mapping phase of Subread. This would prevent taking an unhealthy BAM file to the next step and warn the user of storage-issues.

Kind regards.
Karel
